what_its_for: Metaxalone is a muscle relaxer used to help relieve pain and discomfort caused by muscle strains, sprains, and other muscle injuries. It works by relaxing your muscles and blocking pain signals in your brain. It is usually used together with rest and physical therapy.
how_to_take: Take metaxalone by mouth with or without food. However, taking it with food may increase the amount of medicine your body absorbs and could increase side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and do not take more than directed.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 800 mg (one tablet) taken 3 to 4 times a day. Do not take more than 4 doses in one day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your condition. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store metaxalone at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about local drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metaxalone. Alcohol can increase drowsiness and dizziness and raise the risk of dangerous side effects. Avoid driving a car, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids, anxiety medications, opioid pain relievers, or antihistamines, unless your doctor tells you it is safe.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe nausea or vomiting, unusual tiredness or weakness, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if you feel more confused or dizzy than usual, or if your muscle pain does not improve after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: Metaxalone usually starts to work within 1 hour of taking it. Most people feel relief from muscle pain and stiffness within the first few days of use. It is typically prescribed for short-term use, usually no longer than 2 to 3 weeks. If your pain does not improve, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution. Older adults are more sensitive to the drowsiness and dizziness caused by metaxalone, which can increase the risk of falls and injuries. Pregnant women: Talk to your doctor before using this medication. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Breastfeeding women: It is not known if metaxalone passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: Metaxalone is not recommended for children under 12 years of age. Kidney or liver problems: Do not use metaxalone if you have significant kidney or liver disease. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions before starting this medication.
